answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 40% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the yarrow quorum in the pigment ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the dune history exposes each cut. A farm that captures 81 seats thus pays for 81 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 6 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
